title: A systematic review of possible serious adverse health effects of nicotine replacement therapy | Archives of Toxicology | Springer Nature Link
abstract: In regard to potential serious adverse health effects (SAHEs) associated with long-term use of pharmaceutical NRT products in humans, the United Kingdom’s National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) concluded that “evidence is available from studies with up to 5-year follow-up which suggests that ‘pure’ nicotine, in the form available in NRT products, does not pose a significant health risk” (National Institute for Health and Care Excellence 2013 Smoking harm reduction: gaps in the evidence. Obstet Gynecol 96:967–971")) as providing evidence “that nicotine as present in NRT products does not have an adverse effect on infant weight”, and another (Kapur et al. Toxicol Sci 116(2):364–374")), evaluated evidence from six studies we considered (see CAFs 2, 3, 8, 10, 13 and 14), but reached no overall conclusions, except that “the safety of NRT use during pregnancy has been evaluated in a limited number of short-term human trials, but there is currently no information on the long-term effects of developmental nicotine exposure in humans”.
